# Agent Commands

Every command the `agent` module offers, from its declarations, in order of the resource each acts on. Each command's help says the same.

## Agent

### `lnk agent connect`

Connect your agent to Telegram, Slack, Discord or Signal

```usage
lnk agent connect <connection> [--agent <agent>] [--secret <secret>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `connection`, position 1, string, required: A connection: telegram reads the bot's token from `LNK_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, slack its two tokens from `LNK_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and `LNK_SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, discord its bot's token from `LNK_DISCORD_TOKEN`, signal the agent's number and your own (`lnk agent connect signal` asks), or another connection module's
- `--secret`, string, link-id: The bot token's secret, by its ID, secret:<id>, which the connection's service is given to pass, on an agent a cloud hosts; here the connection reads its token as it says

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent create`

Make another agent, and start it (--agent <name> then picks it)

```usage
lnk agent create <name> [place] [--cloud <cloud>] [--foreground] [--from <from>] [--here] [--let-sleep] [--no-sandbox] [--on <on>] [--sandbox <sandbox>] [--spec <spec>] [--yes] [--zone <zone>] [field flags]
```

- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account
- `--foreground`, boolean: Run it in this terminal instead of in the background
- `--from`, string: An agent to start from, by the name of its archive, with its instructions, skills and settings: a cloud that hosts agents makes it from one it lists
- `--here`, boolean: This machine
- `--let-sleep`, boolean: Let the machine sleep while it runs, this start alone: the next start keeps it awake again unless its specification's `[run] let_sleep` says otherwise
- `name`, position 1, string, required: Its name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter; not here or all, which are Link's words
- `--no-sandbox`, boolean: Run with no sandbox, from now on, until a start with --sandbox: the harness can then read your whole home folder (documents, SSH keys, browser data) and write outside its own. The only way to run without one, never implied by --yes. Available on a computer or box; refused where trusted machine policy forbids it (`unsandboxed = false` in agents.toml) or policy cannot be trusted
- `--on`, string: A machine
- `place`, position 2, string: A machine, a cloud account, or here: short for --on <machine>, --cloud <cloud> or --here
- `--sandbox`, path: A sandbox file, a TOML file of what you grant the agent whichever harness runs it (`lnk agent show --permissions` shows it): kept with its settings, in place of what `lnk agent permission add` and `remove` wrote. It runs in its sandbox from now on; given alone, as `--sandbox own`, it only runs in its own sandbox again, after --no-sandbox
- `--spec`, path: A specification file, a TOML file of its opinions over Link's, its field flags laid over it (`lnk agent spec show` prints the whole): kept with its settings, read at every start
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask
- `--zone`, string: A region or zone of the cloud

It reads the [`agent` specification](../../../../config/specs/agent.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `agent.life-agent-entry`.

### `lnk agent delete`

Delete an agent here for good: its settings, harnesses and service, and its files after asking

```usage
lnk agent delete <name> [--delete-files] [--yes]
```

- `--delete-files`, boolean: Delete its files folder too, when it's its own
- `name`, position 1, string, required: An agent (`lnk agent list`)
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent disconnect`

Disconnect your agent from a connection

```usage
lnk agent disconnect <connection> [--agent <agent>]
```

It takes `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]. It takes `connection`, position 1, string, required: A connection: telegram, slack, discord, signal, or another connection module's. It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent list`

List every agent, here and on each of your boxes

```usage
lnk agent list [--here] [--json] [--refresh]
```

- `--here`, boolean: Only this machine's agents, without asking your boxes
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--refresh`, boolean: Ask your clouds for boxes made on your other computers too, not only those this one knows

It answers `agent.life-agents`.

### `lnk agent migrate`

Bring an agent you already have under Link, keeping its harness: OpenClaw, Hermes or DeepSeek, installed here outside Link

```usage
lnk agent migrate [--agent <agent>] [--clean] [--harness <harness>] [--yes]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--clean`, boolean: Once your agent answers under Link: remove the original install, every file of it named first
- `--harness`, string: The harness to bring in, when more than one is installed: openclaw, hermes or deepseek
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent move`

Move an agent to one of your boxes, a cloud, or back here

```usage
lnk agent move [place] [--agent <agent>] [--cloud <cloud>] [--here] [--image <image>] [--on <on>] [--yes] [--zone <zone>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account
- `--here`, boolean: This machine
- `--image`, string: A new box in the cloud account TO, from one of your images there (`lnk box image list`): the agent moves onto a box already set up
- `--on`, string: A machine
- `place`, position 1, string: A machine, a cloud account, or here: short for --on <machine>, --cloud <cloud> or --here
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask
- `--zone`, string: A region or zone of the cloud

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent restart`

Stop your existing agent, then start it in the background with its saved settings

```usage
lnk agent restart [--agent <agent>]
```

It takes `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]. It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent show`

Show everything about this agent

```usage
lnk agent show [name] [--agent <agent>] [--harness <harness>] [--instructions] [--json] [--permissions]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--harness`, string: A harness (`lnk agent harness list`) whose needs --permissions shows [default: your agent's]
- `--instructions`, boolean: Show the prompt your agent's model gets, exactly as its harness sends it
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `name`, position 1, string: An agent (`lnk agent list`): what `lnk agent show` shows of it, as typed blocks with --json
- `--permissions`, boolean: Show what your agent may do beyond its harness's home, here

It answers `agent.life-agent-entry`.

### `lnk agent start`

Start your agent (Link Harness by default), in the background

```usage
lnk agent start [--agent <agent>] [--all] [--foreground] [--let-sleep] [--no-sandbox] [--sandbox <sandbox>] [--spec <spec>] [--yes] [field flags]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--all`, boolean: Start every agent here, each as its own start would, in the background
- `--foreground`, boolean: Run it in this terminal instead of in the background
- `--let-sleep`, boolean: Let the machine sleep while it runs, this start alone: the next start keeps it awake again unless its specification's `[run] let_sleep` says otherwise
- `--no-sandbox`, boolean: Run with no sandbox, from now on, until a start with --sandbox: the harness can then read your whole home folder (documents, SSH keys, browser data) and write outside its own. The only way to run without one, never implied by --yes. Available on a computer or box; refused where trusted machine policy forbids it (`unsandboxed = false` in agents.toml) or policy cannot be trusted
- `--sandbox`, path: A sandbox file, a TOML file of what you grant the agent whichever harness runs it (`lnk agent show --permissions` shows it): kept with its settings, in place of what `lnk agent permission add` and `remove` wrote. It runs in its sandbox from now on; given alone, as `--sandbox own`, it only runs in its own sandbox again, after --no-sandbox
- `--spec`, path: A specification file, a TOML file of its opinions over Link's, its field flags laid over it (`lnk agent spec show` prints the whole): kept with its settings, read at every start
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It reads the [`agent` specification](../../../../config/specs/agent.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `core.report`.

## Chat

### `lnk agent chat compact`

Compact the current conversation

```usage
lnk agent chat compact [--agent <agent>] [--chat <chat>] [--json]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--chat`, string: The chat to act on
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs

It answers `agent.chat-turn`.

### `lnk agent chat export`

Export the current conversation

```usage
lnk agent chat export [--agent <agent>] [--chat <chat>] [--format <format>] [--json]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--chat`, string: The chat to act on
- `--format`, string: Rewrite every conversation in this format, as `[storage] conversations` names one
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs

It answers `agent.chat-turn`.

### `lnk agent chat fork`

Copy the chat before an owner's message into a fresh Link chat, preserving the original

```usage
lnk agent chat fork <chat> [--agent <agent>] --before <before>
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--before`, integer, required: The sequence number of the owner's message to edit; the copy ends before it
- `chat`, position 1, string, required: A chat (`lnk agent chat list`), such as `link:main`

It answers `agent.chat`.

### `lnk agent chat get`

Get one value of the current conversation: its goal

```usage
lnk agent chat get <field> [--agent <agent>] [--chat <chat>] [--json]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--chat`, string: The chat to act on
- `field`, position 1, one of `goal`, required: The value to get: `goal`, the condition the chat works toward
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs

It answers `agent.chat-turn`.

### `lnk agent chat list`

List this agent's Link conversations, when its harness supports typed history

```usage
lnk agent chat list [--agent <agent>] [--json]
```

It takes `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]. It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `agent.chat-list`.

### `lnk agent chat send`

Send one message to your agent on Link's own connection

```usage
lnk agent chat send [--action <action>] [--agent <agent>] [--aside] [--chat <chat>] [--cloud <cloud>] [--connection <connection>] [--json] [--member <member>] [--message <message>] [--queue] [--steer] [--stream-json] [--team <team>] [--to <to>]
```

- `--action`, string: Run one agent action, such as model:show, then exit
- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--aside`, boolean: Ask it as a side question, answered apart and kept out of the conversation
- `--chat`, string: A chat (`lnk agent chat list`), such as `link:<name>` [default: main; with --team, one for that team; with --to, the owner's chat to reply in, or the chat for a teammate's reply]
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account, as `lnk cloud list` names it
- `--connection`, string: With --to owner: where to message the owner, a connected service, or `cli` for this computer's `lnk agent chat`
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--member`, string: With --team: a unique member name within the team [default: its selected lead]
- `--message`, `-m`, string: Send this one message, print the answer and exit. On the command line, other processes here can read it; on stdin they can't
- `--queue`, boolean: Send it after the answer being written
- `--steer`, boolean: Let it join the answer being written
- `--stream-json`, boolean: Stream each event as a line of JSON for a remote client: its text as it comes, then how it ended
- `--team`, string: Message this team through its lead (`lnk agent team list`), or team@account for hosting
- `--to`, string: Send as the agent: `owner`, or a teammate as `teammate:<name or ID>`

It answers `agent.chat-event`.

### `lnk agent chat set`

Set one value of the current conversation: its goal, its name, or whether it shows each tool call

```usage
lnk agent chat set <field> [value] [--agent <agent>] [--chat <chat>] [--clear] [--json]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--chat`, string: The chat to act on
- `--clear`, boolean: Clear the goal instead of setting it
- `field`, position 1, one of `goal`, `name`, `verbose`, required: The value to set: `goal`, a condition the chat works toward, `name`, the conversation's name, or `verbose`, whether it shows each tool call
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `value`, position 2, string: Its new value: a goal, a name, or on or off

It answers `agent.chat-turn`.

### `lnk agent chat show`

Print one of your agent's chats as you'd read it, wherever it's kept

```usage
lnk agent chat show <chat> [--agent <agent>] [--json] [--status]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `chat`, position 1, string, required: A chat (`lnk agent chat list`), such as `link:main` or `telegram:123456789`
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--status`, boolean: Show the chat's current conversation's model and usage, as its running harness says, instead of what was said

It answers `agent.chat`.

### `lnk agent chat start`

Start a fresh live conversation with your agent; --chat selects an existing named chat

```usage
lnk agent chat start [--agent <agent>] [--chat <chat>] [--json] [--message <message>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--chat`, string: Continue this named chat instead of opening a fresh one
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--message`, `-m`, string: Open the chat with this first message, then keep talking

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent chat stop`

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]

- `--member`, string, required: Your hosted agent's name or permanent ID
- `team`, position 1, string, required: The team (`lnk agent team list`)

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent team leave`

End your hosted agent's membership in another account's team

```usage
lnk agent team leave <team> [--account <account>] [--cloud <cloud>] --member <member>
```

- `--account`, string: A Link account, by its username or ID
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account, as `lnk cloud list` names it
- `--member`, string, required: Your hosted agent's name or permanent ID
- `team`, position 1, string, required: The team (`lnk agent team list`)

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent team list`

List the teams, each member's purpose and what it reaches

```usage
lnk agent team list [--agent <agent>] [--json]
```

It takes `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]. It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `agent.teams-listed`.

### `lnk agent team move`

Move a team with all its own members and its shared folder

```usage
lnk agent team move <team> [place] [--agent <agent>] [--cloud <cloud>] [--here] [--on <on>] [--yes] [--zone <zone>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account
- `--here`, boolean: This machine
- `--on`, string: A machine
- `place`, position 2, string: A machine, a cloud account, or here: short for --on <machine>, --cloud <cloud> or --here
- `team`, position 1, string, required: A team (`lnk agent team list`), as team@cloud when a cloud hosts it
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask
- `--zone`, string: A region or zone of the cloud

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent team remove`

Remove an agent from a team

```usage
lnk agent team remove <team> [--cloud <cloud>] --member <member>
```

- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account, as `lnk cloud list` names it
- `--member`, string, required: An agent (`lnk agent list`)
- `team`, position 1, string, required: A team (`lnk agent team list`)

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent team restore`

Restore a hosted team's shared folder from its backup

```usage
lnk agent team restore <team> [--agent <agent>] [--cloud <cloud>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account, as `lnk cloud list` names it
- `team`, position 1, string, required: A hosted team (`lnk agent team list`)

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent team show`

Show a team, or with --member one of its members: its agent, purpose, state and what it reaches here, or accepted membership on a hosting cloud

```usage
lnk agent team show <team> [--agent <agent>] [--cloud <cloud>] [--json] [--member <member>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account, as `lnk cloud list` names it
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--member`, string: One member of the team
- `team`, position 1, string, required: A team (`lnk agent team list`)

It answers `agent.teams-hosted-shown`.

### `lnk agent team start`

Start the team's members, keeping their permanent identities

```usage
lnk agent team start <team> [--agent <agent>] [--cloud <cloud>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account, as `lnk cloud list` names it
- `team`, position 1, string, required: Team whose members to start

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent team stop`

Stop the team's members, preserving agents, identities and files

```usage
lnk agent team stop <team> [--agent <agent>] [--cloud <cloud>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--cloud`, string: A cloud account, as `lnk cloud list` names it
- `team`, position 1, string, required: Team whose members to stop

It answers `core.report`.

## Tool

### `lnk agent tool add`

Give your agent a tool: memory, web, browser, desktop, scheduler, run, file, code or your own

```usage
lnk agent tool add <tool> [--agent <agent>] [--yes]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `tool`, position 1, string, required: The tool: memory (search over its files and conversations, and notes), web (pages, and a search with a Brave Search or Tavily key, from `BRAVE_API_KEY` or `TAVILY_API_KEY`, or asked for), browser, desktop, scheduler, run, file, code, or another tool's name
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent tool list`

List the tools your agent has

```usage
lnk agent tool list [--agent <agent>] [--json] [--request <request>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--request`, string: JSON request file (default: standard input)

It answers `agent.tool-namespaces`.

### `lnk agent tool remove`

Take a tool from your agent (what it kept stays)

```usage
lnk agent tool remove <tool> [--agent <agent>]
```

It takes `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]. It takes `tool`, position 1, string, required: The tool: memory, web, or another tool's name. It answers `core.report`.

## Web

### `lnk agent web fetch`

Fetch a web page

```usage
lnk agent web fetch [--agent <agent>] [--json] [--request <request>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--request`, string: JSON request file (default: standard input)

It answers `web-tool.page`.

### `lnk agent web search`

Search the web

```usage
lnk agent web search [--agent <agent>] [--json] [--request <request>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--request`, string: JSON request file (default: standard input)

It answers `web-tool.results`.

## Webhook

### `lnk agent webhook create`

Create a webhook, and print its address and its secret, once

```usage
lnk agent webhook create <name> [--agent <agent>] [--questions-per-day <questions-per-day>] [--sender <sender>]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `name`, position 1, string, required: Its name: what your agent sees it's from (webhook:<name>)
- `--questions-per-day`, integer: How many questions ({"question": "..."}) it may ask you on your chats a day [default: 20]
- `--sender`, one of `link`, `github`: The scheme that signs the posts: link or github

It answers `agent.webhook-secret`.

### `lnk agent webhook delete`

Delete a webhook: its address takes no more posts, and its secrets are forgotten

```usage
lnk agent webhook delete <name> [--agent <agent>]
```

It takes `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]. It takes `name`, position 1, string, required: The webhook. It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk agent webhook list`

List the agent's webhooks: each name, who signs it and its address, never its secret

```usage
lnk agent webhook list [--agent <agent>] [--json]
```

It takes `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]. It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `agent.webhook`.

### `lnk agent webhook rotate`

Give a webhook a new secret, printed once

```usage
lnk agent webhook rotate <name> [--agent <agent>] [--done]
```

- `--agent`, `-a`, agent ID: The agent, by its ID, agent:<id>; on the command line its name too, which is looked up in your agents and sent as its ID [default: the only one here]
- `--done`, boolean: Its sender has the new secret: stop taking the previous one now, and make none
- `name`, position 1, string, required: The webhook

It answers `agent.webhook-secret`.
